answer: Mount Everest is 8,848.86 metres (about 29,032 feet) above sea level. Nepal and China announced this as the official height on 8 December 2020 [1][2]. The two countries had disagreed about the height for a long time. The new figure came from survey teams from both countries who reached the summit in 2019 and 2020 and measured it with GPS and trigonometry [1][2]. It is a little higher than earlier official figures. Those were 8,848 m from the 1954 Survey of India, which counted the snow on top, and 8,844.43 m from China in 2005, which measured to the rock beneath the snow [2]. Everest is the highest mountain above sea level. The Challenger Deep is about 10,935 m deep, so the ocean's deepest point is roughly 2 km farther below sea level than Everest's summit is above it.
